methods.description: Count the permitted choices at each stage and multiply; retain the choices when repeats are allowed, and explain why each first choice pairs with every later choice.
Divide the known total by the product of the known stage counts to find the missing count.
Calculate and compare the stage products for different cases; subtract old from new when an increase is requested.

sourceReview.observation: Actually read the complete multistage/tree introduction and complete three-coin investigation. The blank scaffold explicitly links the fundamental counting principle to2×2×2=8 outcomes. Tree drawing and probability questions are separate tasks; the counting principle extends beyond two stages.
sourceReview.adjustments: Used this existing Stage5 extension for three-stage outfits/codes/menus and retained longer repeated-position products in good assessments. No tree-drawing example, probability multiplication or factorial shorthand was added.

sourceReview.observation: Actually read the complete opening counting principle, all six everyday counting scaffolds, Box Method, both worked code examples, adjoining code practice and closing KeyIdea. The source explicitly identifies elementary clothing/menu/code counts as prior probability knowledge. Its first number-plate example says2letters/4digits and draws26,26,10,10,10,10 but prints26²×10³=676000: that printed expression matches only3digits, so it is not adopted. Its alternating-digit example correctly gives4×5×4×5×4=1600. There is no filled missing-stage or menu-change comparison example in this selected original context.
sourceReview.adjustments: Later-stage wording/setout only: Example1 adapts the actual letter/digit code working to one letter/two digits and the restricted-vowel/last-digit counts5,10,3, with explicit repeat permission and no powers formula. Examples2/3 adapt the available everyday restaurant scaffold by solving the same product backwards and comparing changed products. These are honest elementary derivations from the counting principle, not purported identical source worked examples. No later ordered-selection formula, factorial/permutation/combination notation or alternating-five-position task is taught.

substantiveCorrections: Clarified that the product rule assumes every first choice may pair with each available later choice, and corrected the repetition fact so mixed letter/digit positions need not have equal option counts.
Corrected quiz.q9 options[1]/[2] explanations:12/15 are valid smaller increases, not evidence of an invented counting misconception.

Added four concise source-adapted examples covering stage counts with a useful repeat/restriction contrast, missing stage count and comparison of changed products. All19practice items and all9quiz questions/options/results/IDs remain unchanged.
